subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.

spec.name: Longspear Railgun Carrier
spec.description: A six-wheeled low-poly sci-fi military carrier with a long electromagnetic railgun on its roof, braced on four deployed hydraulic stabiliser legs.
spec.layout: Long armoured wedge-nosed hull, 2.6 m wide and 8 m long, with the cab and sensor mast at the front (+Z) and the railgun cradle at the rear deck. The railgun barrel is a long twin-rail assembly pointing forward (+Z) over the cab roof, raised at about 10 degrees. Six big chunky wheels on three axles (front, middle, rear) sit under the hull sides, with hull-colour fenders. Four stabiliser legs fold out sideways and down from the hull at the middle and rear axles, with flat round footpads planted on the floor, and these pads are the lowest points along with the wheels. The hull is faceted dark gunmetal with olive-drab panelling, yellow hazard trim on the legs and pads, and cyan glow strips and capacitor cores. Everything is blocky, chamfered and angular. Panel lines, rivets, decals, stencil numbers and hazard stripes are painted or textured on the surfaces.

parts.builds: The armoured hull: a lofted faceted body with a sloped wedge nose and flat rear, a stepped deck, side skirts with panelled paint (panelled/mottle camo in hull and armor greens, darker underside), a cab with glass windscreen slabs and side windows, headlights, a front tow hook and bumper plate, rear cargo hatch, exhaust stacks, side hatches with stencil numbers and hazard decals, an antenna mast (joint mast) with a radar dish and blinking red light, and cyan glow strips. Includes the underbody tub and axle housings (stubs reaching to each axle mount). Does not include wheels, legs or the gun.
parts.attaches: Carries all joints through body. Cab roof at cabRoof, deck at hullTop, an empty cradle seat at gunCradle for the gun part to build onto, leg anchor pads at legAnchorMidL/legAnchorRearL and mirrored, axle housings at axleFront/axleMid/axleRear.

parts.builds: Six heavy chunky wheels, each one a faceted rubber tyre (lathe of 10-12 segments) with deep tread blocks, a steel hub with lug nuts, a gunmetal rim ring and a small cyan hub light, plus a fender arch over each wheel in hull colour with a mud-flap. Mirrored left and right, each wheel on its own wheelXX joint with the axle along x. Tyre radius 0.7 and width 0.6, so the wheel bottoms touch y=0. Includes short steel axle shafts and brake discs between hull and wheel.
parts.attaches: At axleFront, axleMid and axleRear on each side (x = ±1.45), axle stubs meeting the hull housings at x = ±1.2.

parts.builds: Four deployed stabiliser legs, extended sideways and down. Each leg has a wall-mounted box bracket at the hull anchor, a horizontal outrigger box beam going out to x=±2.6, a diagonal hydraulic strut with a chrome piston rod and a yellow-black hazard-striped sleeve (stripes texture), a vertical telescoping post, and a wide octagonal footpad (radius 0.45) with ribbed underside, bolts and a yellow rim. Pads touch y=0. Knee joints are rendered as hinge blocks with pins; cyan status lights on each leg; stencil warning decals. Mirrored on the midship and rear anchors, with the legML etc. joints at the anchors.
parts.attaches: Starts at legAnchorMidL/legAnchorRearL (x=±1.3) and mirrored on the right; reaches out beyond the wheels (x up to ±2.9) and down to y=0.

parts.builds: The rear half of the railgun: the cradle and rotating turntable base on the deck, two side trunnion arms, the big breech housing at gunBreech with an angular armoured capacitor bank (blocky boxes with a glowing cyan core strips and vents), cable bundles (thin sweeps) running to the hull, an ammo magazine box with warnRed hazard decals, a yellow-black trim, and the start of the twin rails from the breech to z=1.0. Rides the gunMount joint (elevated about 10 degrees).
parts.attaches: Sits on the cradle seat at gunCradle on the hull; rails continue to the barrel part at z=1.0 on the gun axis (x=0, rails at x=±0.17 and y offset to the gunMount line).

parts.builds: The long barrel: two parallel flat gunmetal rails (extruded or box beams) with a gap between them, held by about 6 spaced rectangular cross-braces and clamps with bolts, glowing cyan inner energy lines along the rails, a heat-tinted steel paint towards the muzzle, a chunky muzzle brake with angular fins, white range markings, a targeting sensor box on top, and a red tip light. It lies along the gun axis tilted about 10 degrees up and runs from z=1.0 to the muzzle at gunMuzzle (z~5.2), over the cab roof clear of the mast.
parts.attaches: Starts where railgunBody's rails end at z=1.0 (gun axis), ends at gunMuzzle. Rides the gunMount joint.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning a function to build the railgun's rear half, keeping it concise but detailed, with parts positioned in model space along the gun's tilted axis using the gunMount joint and bone reference.

I work out a gun-local coordinate helper that maps axis-aligned coordinates to model space by rotating around the X axis to match the 10° elevation, using a quaternion so parts can be placed consistently along the barrel direction. Then I sketch out local z-positions for the breech, rails, and rear box limits relative to the pivot, checking that elevation doesn't push the front too high relative to the box's max height.

Now I'm planning the turntable and cradle geometry: a non-tilted cylindrical turntable sitting on the deck with a rim and bearing ring, and cradle side cheeks as boxes flanking the trunnion that will connect up to the pivot.

For the trunnion and breech, I'm figuring out pin cylinders at the pivot axis and a chamfered breech housing built from an extruded octagon profile aligned with the gun's local x/y axes so it tilts correctly with the barrel.

Now I'm adding capacitor banks on the breech sides with glowing cyan strips, a magazine box with hazard-stripe decals behind the breech, and cable sweeps running from the breech rear to the hull deck attached to the gun mount bone.

Still adding rail geometry...

I'm importing a glow kit and setting up a box helper that uses size, color, and local position offsets. I'm planning to use a mottled armor paint texture blending the armor and hull colors for the body panels.

Now I'm figuring out the warning decal placement — a red svg texture with chevrons and "AMMO" text mapped onto the magazine's side face, computing the right quaternion rotation so the plane aligns with the gun's local X axis.

Writing bolt and breech geometry...

Still placing capacitor glow strips and vents, then I'm laying out the rail geometry with cross braces and cyan accent lines, and starting on the top capacitor and magazine placement.

Adding magazine box details...

Routing cables from the capacitor banks down to the hull deck with slight curvature, then confirming the rear end sits within the model bounds before finalizing coordinates.

I'm sketching out the hull-building function, using the existing body and mast joints to position the parts and boxes concisely.

I'm working through loft station placement along the z-axis, balancing hull width against wheel clearance, and considering using a catmull-smooth loft for the hull's cross-sections with varying heights and widths from tail to nose.

For materials, I'm planning to import panelled and metal helpers from the clockwork kit to give the hull a mottled armor finish, then laying out the vertical positions for the hull body and deck mounts.

I'm reworking the heights now: lowering the hull top to 2.0, centering the main loft body around y=1.5 with a 1.0 span, and placing the cab box above it from 2.0 to 2.5 so it sits correctly relative to the gun cradle and deck mounts.

Next I'm adding the underbody tub box beneath the hull, axle housing boxes positioned symmetrically along x for the suspension, and a tilted windscreen slab on the cab front using rotation to get the sloped angle right.

Then I'm placing side window glass panels on the cab sides, a bumper plate at the front, a small torus tow hook, and glowing headlight boxes with emissive white material.

Now I'm positioning the headlights near the bumper, adding a rear cargo hatch with handle detail, and planning exhaust stacks and a gun breech placement near the back of the vehicle.

For the sides, I'm adding stenciled hatch panels using SVG textures with hazard borders and numbering, placed on planes aligned to the hull's width.

Now I'm working out skirt placement between the wheel wells, positioning thin box segments on either side of the hull at z offsets that clear the wheel radius zones around each axle.

For the leg anchor pads, I'm noticing they'd overlap the wheel geometry at the default position, so I'm shrinking the pad dimensions and nudging them to sit clear of the wheel's footprint while still aligning with the legs.

Now I'm turning to the mast assembly on the cab roof - a thin pole, a dish built from a flattened cone shape, a glowing red beacon sphere on top, plus some small sensor boxes, making sure it all clears the gun's swing radius.

I'm also planning cyan glow strips along the hull sides and nose edge, plus a diagonal hazard-stripe texture applied to the bumper plate using an SVG pattern for the yellow stripes.

Now I'm adding stepped deck plates for the rear armor and cab step, along with small vent grills, a roof hatch cylinder, deck lines, and an octagonal gunmetal cradle seat with a thin glowing cyan ring. I'm keeping the color scheme restricted to the defined palette and building out the SVG texture strings for these details.

Writing hull material functions...

Adding more loft stations with smooth transitions between nose and cab, adjusting cab box position to y 1.9-2.5 so it sits flush over the body without gaps, and placing a windscreen on the cab front near z3.

I'll skip the sloped glacis piece for simplicity, keeping the triangle budget reasonable. I'm planning decal textures for the body using SVG text stencils and a hazard triangle decal on the rear, pulling in rivet and glow details from existing kits, then writing out the plane placement and hatch box geometry code.

Working through placement math for the side hatch box and skirt so they don't overlap — adjusting y-positions and heights for both until the ranges fit cleanly.
